Velyki Lazy Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Velyki Lazy, Ukraine

Not demolished. Presumably established in the 19th century, this cemetery's oldest gravestone dates to 1877, its latest to 1938. Jews are believed to have arrived in the late 18th century; population reached 43 (12%) by 1851 and 83 by 1880, then declined to 46 by 1910, 31 by 1921 (Czechoslovak period), and 26 by 1930. Hungarian forces arrived in March 1939, drafting some Jews into forced labor battalions by 1941, with others sent to the Eastern Front where most perished. Population reached 27 by 1941; families without Hungarian citizenship were expelled that year to Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered. Remaining Jews were deported to Auschwitz in late May 1944. No Jews live in the town today.
